title: --here and Search Only in find nothing when the folder was given with .. in its path, through a link, or in another letter case
problem:
Found by the review of the whole branch (20 Nov), in which one reviewer read all the improvements together through one lens and a second reviewer tried to refute each finding against the code. Nothing was run in that review: every finding was traced by reading. [here-path-with-dotdot-finds-nothing] `--here` with a PATH that has `..` in it searches nothing on Linux and macOS (a linked folder inside a search location fails the same way). The finder's scenario: Home is the search location. In ~/src/app run `fffinder ../lib --query parser --here` (or `fffinder .. --here` and type a word; the same when a running copy takes the launch, and with `--pick`). The window opens the right folder and lists its items, Search Only in "lib" is on, and the search says No Results although files in the folder match. Without `--here` the same words find them, and `cd ../lib; fffinder --here --query parser` works, because the shell's folder comes without `..`. Expected: the folder's matches, as the manual says of `--here`. Windows is not affected: std::path::absolute resolves `..` there, while on POSIX it keeps it. The root cause is older than the branch (the toolbar's Search Only in button fails the same way in a window opened with `fffinder ..`), but `--here` is the branch's documented way to get there in one command. Same outcome for a PATH that is a symlink inside a search location (follow_symlinks is off by default, so the index has nothing under the link's name). The code path: src/lib.rs:44-45 and 336-341 (start_location: std::path::absolute keeps `..`, the result becomes Location::Folder); src/lib.rs:54-57 (the same path is handed to a running copy); src/lib.rs:148-155 and src/finder/mod.rs:1181-1194 (open_request navigates to it, then search_here); src/finder/mod.rs:2157-2162 and 2194-2205 (the scope of the search is current_folder() as spelled); crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:818-822 (root_spelling returns None because `/home/u/src/app/../lib` starts with the root as text, so nothing is canonicalized); engine.rs:134-140 and 1058-1065 (in_base keeps `app/../lib`, folder_glob at 2756-2769 writes it as the glob `app/../lib/**`, which no indexed path matches); engine.rs:1112-1118 (in_scope: path.starts_with(scope) is false for every hit). The contents search does the same at engine.rs:1394-1400 and 1517-1521. Their evidence: Traced end to end in the snapshot; nothing on the way cleans the path. By reading only, nothing was built or run.

1. The path keeps its `..`. src/args.rs:95 and 109-115 store PATH untouched. src/lib.rs:46-47: `let folder = args.path.clone().or_else(|| shell_folder(args.term)); let start = start_location(folder.as_ref(), &config);`. src/lib.rs:338-341: `let path = std::path::absolute(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.clone()); if path.is_dir() { return Location::Folder(path); }`. On POSIX std::path::absolute keeps `..` (std docs; ignore-0.4.34/src/incremental.rs:584-599 calls it and then pops ParentDir itself, for that reason). So `../lib` run in /home/u/src/app becomes Location::Folder("/home/u/src/app/../lib"), and is_dir() is true, so the window lists the folder.
2. The hand-off is the same: src/lib.rs:54-57 sends `std::path::absolute(p)`; src/server/mod.rs:627-631 checks only is_absolute; src/finder/mod.rs:1182-1183 `self.navigate(Location::Folder(path.to_path_buf()), window, cx)`, then 1192-1194 search_here.
3. The window keeps the spelling: src/finder/mod.rs:798 `history: History::new(start)`; 2157-2162 `SearchScope::Folder => self.current_folder().map(Path::to_path_buf)`; 2194 and 2203-2205 put it in SearchRequest.scope; content_search (4203-4205) passes it on unchanged.
4. The engine takes it as text. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:820-822: `if indexes.roots.iter().any(|r| scope.starts_with(&r.path)) { return None; }`. Path::starts_with goes by components and `..` is one, so /home/u/src/app/../lib starts with /home/u and canonicalize (823) is never reached.
5. engine.rs:135-137 in_base: `Ok(rest) => base.join(rest)` keeps `src/app/../lib`. 1061-1065 hand it to folder_glob, and 2758-2767 write each component, a `/`, then `**`: the glob is `src/app/../lib/**`. It is pushed as Constraint::Glob at 1134, 1156 and 1207. fff-search-0.11.0 src/index/constraints.rs:517-521 compiles it with globset as it is, and src/score.rs:611-615 returns nothing when no path passes: `Some(_) => { return vec![]; }`. No indexed path contains `..`.
6. Even a returned hit would be dropped: engine.rs:1113-1114 `Some(scope) => path.starts_with(scope) && path != scope` is false for /home/u/src/lib/parser.rs.
7. Contents search is the same: engine.rs:1342 (root_spelling again), 1394-1400 (same glob), 1439 `query.constraints.push(Constraint::Glob(glob))`, 1517-1521 `!path.starts_with(scope)` -> continue.

What I looked for and did not find: a canonicalize or lexical cleanup anywhere between the arguments and SearchRequest.scope (rg for canonicalize|absolute over src/ finds only lib.rs:56 and 338 and an unrelated src/system.rs:367). A test that pins it: no path in tests/, src/ or crates/ contains `..`, and every --here test passes fx.path(..) or fx.tree() (tests/finder.rs:1836-1960, tests/server.rs:348).

The finder's side claims hold. `cd ../lib; fffinder --here` works because the folder then comes from getcwd. `fff gui` and `fff pick` are not affected (nu/fff.nu:133 and 165 `path expand`; tests/nu_module.rs:88-89). A trailing slash, which absolute also keeps, is harmless (components drop it). A symlinked PATH inside a location fails by the same lines: step 4 returns None, the glob is `link/**`, and with follow_symlinks false (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:370) the index holds nothing under the link.

Age: 66c919b has the same start_location (src/lib.rs:321-323) and the same early return (engine.rs:458-461), so the Search Only in button already failed in a window opened with `fffinder ..`. 3836a5e adds the documented one-command way in (docs/manual.md:79 promises the folder's matches).

Not in query-scope-from-cli.json, scoped-search-special-folder-names.json, strict-check-scope-relative.json or final-pass-notes.md.

Test that shows it on Linux: in engine.rs searches_a_folder (4794), search `readme` with scope Some(dir.join("docs/notes/..")); by the trace it returns 0 hits where 1 is right. [scope-in-another-letter-case-finds-nothing] A folder spelled in another letter case is searched as spelled: `--here` finds nothing on macOS and Windows. The finder's scenario: macOS, home is the search location, the folder on disk is ~/Documents: `fffinder ~/documents --query report --here`. The window lists the folder (the file system ignores case), Search Only in "documents" is on, and the search says No Results. Windows, in PowerShell, which keeps a folder's name as typed: from C:\Users\me run `cd documents`, then `fffinder --here --query report`: the same. Also `"in_folder": true` in POST /v1/open and `scope` in /v1/find with such a spelling; `fff find --here` and `fff search --here` send $env.PWD as it is. Expected: the folder's matches. Only a spelling that differs inside the search location fails: when the search-location part itself differs (`/users/me/Documents`), root_spelling canonicalizes and the search works. As with the `..` finding the weakness is older than the branch (the Search Only in button after Go to Folder with a lowercase path), and `--here` adds the command-line way into it. By reading only; nothing was run on macOS or Windows. The code path: src/lib.rs:44 (shell_folder: std::env::current_dir, which on Windows is the string the shell set), src/lib.rs:336-341 (std::path::absolute keeps the typed case); src/finder/mod.rs:2157-2162 (scope = current_folder()); crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:818-822 (root_spelling: `/Users/me/documents`.starts_with(`/Users/me`) is true, so it returns None before canonicalizing); engine.rs:134-140 (in_base keeps the typed rest); engine.rs:1061-1065 (glob `documents/**`, matched letter for letter: fff-search-0.11.0/src/index/constraints.rs compile_one builds a case-sensitive globset::Glob); engine.rs:1112-1118 (in_scope compares path components exactly, so nothing under `Documents` is in scope). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: Certain by reading: an explicit PATH typed in another letter case on a file system that ignores case. macOS (default APFS): `fffinder ~/documents --query report --here`, first launch or handed to a running copy. Windows: `fffinder C:\Users\me\documents --query report --here` from any shell. The window lists the folder, Search Only in "documents" is on, and the search says No Results. Only a difference inside the search location matters; a difference in the location's own part is repaired by root_spelling.

Not affected: `cd ~/documents; fffinder --here` on macOS, where the folder comes from getcwd in its on-disk spelling, and `fff gui` / `fff pick`, which use `path expand`.

Narrower than the finder says for Windows: the `cd documents` then `fffinder --here` route needs a shell that hands its child the folder as typed. cmd.exe corrects the case on cd (its own help says so). Windows PowerShell 5.1 keeps the typed case as far as I know. I could not establish what PowerShell 7 does. None of this was run. Their evidence: Same code path as the `..` finding, traced in the snapshot; the only difference is the kind of misspelling. By reading only; it cannot be shown on Linux, where another letter case is another folder.

1. The typed case survives. src/lib.rs:338-341: `let path = std::path::absolute(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.clone()); if path.is_dir() { return Location::Folder(path); }`. std::path::absolute does not read the disk on any system, so /Users/me/documents stays as typed, and is_dir() is true where the file system ignores case. The hand-off (src/lib.rs:54-57), src/server/mod.rs:627-631 and src/finder/mod.rs:1182-1183 pass it on unchanged. src/finder/mod.rs:2157-2162 makes it the scope.
2. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:820-822: `if indexes.roots.iter().any(|r| scope.starts_with(&r.path)) { return None; }`. /Users/me/documents starts with /Users/me, so the canonicalize at 823, which would give the on-disk name, is skipped.
3. engine.rs:135-137 `Ok(rest) => base.join(rest)` keeps `documents`; 1061-1065 and 2756-2769 make the glob `documents/**`.
4. The glob is matched letter for letter: fff-search-0.11.0 src/index/constraints.rs:517-521 `globset::Glob::new(pattern).ok().map(|g| g.compile_matcher())` with no options, and globset-0.4.21 src/glob.rs:247-250 has `case_insensitive: false`. The index holds `Documents/...` as the disk names it, so nothing passes, and fff-search-0.11.0 src/score.rs:611-615 returns `vec![]`.
5. engine.rs:1113-1114 `path.starts_with(scope)` compares names exactly on every system, so a hit under `Documents` would be dropped anyway. Contents search: 1394-1400, 1439 and 1517-1521 do the same.

No guard found: nothing between the arguments and the engine reads the folder's real name, and neither fff-search nor the engine has a macOS or Windows branch on this path. No test uses a second spelling of a folder. Not in the done records or final-pass-notes.md; later.md:1226 notes a letter-case gap, but for search locations compared with each other, not for a searched folder.

Older than the branch in the same way as the `..` finding (66c919b engine.rs:458-461), and `fff find --here` / `fff search --here` sending $env.PWD unexpanded is upstream's too (66c919b nu/fff.nu:173 and 237). 3836a5e adds the command-line route.

Severity 2: the visible failure is the same false No Results as in the `..` finding, but the path has to be typed by hand in a case other than the disk's. Tab completion, a dragged path and the macOS working folder all give the on-disk case.

Test to run on a Mac or on Windows: an engine test with a location holding Docs/readme.md, search `readme` with scope root.join("docs"), expect 1 hit; by the trace it returns 0.
proposal: Reproduce each fault first with a test that fails on the trunk. Then fix it. The finder's suggested fixes, as starting points and not checked plans: [here-path-with-dotdot-finds-nothing] Clean the folder where it comes in: in start_location (src/lib.rs:338), for the hand-off path (src/lib.rs:56) and in Finder::open_request, use the folder's real spelling when it exists (std::fs::canonicalize on Unix, std::path::absolute elsewhere). The shell's folder already arrives that way. Alternatively in the engine: have root_spelling canonicalize also when the scope starts with a root as text and return the respelled path when it differs, and use the same path in indexes_for. [scope-in-another-letter-case-finds-nothing] The same place as the `..` finding: take the folder's on-disk spelling when it comes in. In the engine, the smallest change is in root_spelling (engine.rs:818-832): drop the early return, canonicalize the scope, and return the root-spelled path (r.path joined with the rest after r.canonical) whenever it differs from what was given; the recursion in search and grep_cancellable ends because the second call gets the path it would return.
original_test_plan: The finder's test ideas: [here-path-with-dotdot-finds-nothing] In crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, searches_a_folder: add a search for `readme` with scope Some(dir.join("docs/notes/..")) and expect 1 hit; today 0. In tests/finder.rs: open_request(Some(&fx.path("Projects/atlas/..")), Some("atlas"), true, ..) and expect Project Atlas.txt among ui.names(); today the list is empty. A unit test in src/lib.rs: start_location(Some(&dir.join("a/..")), &config) is Location::Folder(dir). [scope-in-another-letter-case-finds-nothing] An engine test for macOS and Windows only (#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", windows))]): a root with Docs/readme.md, search `readme` with scope root.join("docs"), expect readme.md; today nothing. To have one that fails on Linux too, take the respelling out into a function that is given the canonical path (respell(scope, canonical, roots)) and test that `/r/docs` with canonical `/r/Docs` comes back as `/r/Docs`. Why the existing tests miss it: [here-path-with-dotdot-finds-nothing] Every test hands open_request, start_location and the second launch a clean absolute fixture path (tests/finder.rs a_search_sent_with_here_stays_in_the_folder, here_is_the_folder_the_window_goes_to, a_window_opened_with_here_shows_nothing_from_outside_its_folder; tests/server.rs a_second_launch_hands_here_to_the_running_window passes fx.tree()). The real-app runs in the record used `Projects`. The Nushell tests go through `path expand`, which resolves `..`, so `fff gui` and `fff pick` are not affected and hide it. [scope-in-another-letter-case-finds-nothing] Nothing ran on macOS or Windows, and every fixture uses one spelling of its folders. On Linux a folder in another letter case doesn't exist, so no test there can show it. The symlink respelling that root_spelling does is tested (protocol.md's /private/var case); the case inside a root is not.
original_risks: This is a fix late in the branch: keep it to the fault. Every test on the trunk has to keep passing, and the improvements involved (query-scope-from-cli, scoped-search-special-folder-names) have tests that pin the behaviour around the fault: read their done records in /home/user/polish-tools/done/ before changing the functions they changed.

verifier.claim_check: A second reviewer traced the same path and confirmed it; neither ran anything. Reproduce before changing anything; if a test shows the fault is not there, write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.

orchestrator_notes: This fault was in the app before this branch, at least in part: write a normal `Changelog (Fixed):` paragraph for what a user of the last release would notice. The full findings, with the second reviewer's evidence line by line, are in /home/user/polish-tools/review/*.md and *.json (search for the finding ids in brackets). The review read the branch at 7e8df53; other changes have landed since, so read the functions as they are now. 'query-scope-from-cli' (3836a5e) added --here; its done record lists every way a folder comes in with a search (a first launch, a launch handed to a running fffinder, --pick, POST /v1/open with in_folder, and the Nushell commands, which already expand the path). The root cause is older than the branch: write a normal Changelog (Fixed) paragraph. Keep the change where the folder comes in, as the finders suggest, unless the engine's own `root_spelling` is clearly the smaller and safer place; two other changes are in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs right now.
